newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent to rise, eyes $18.62-$18.77 gap.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent to rise, eyes $18.62-$18.77 gap.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - APRIL 15 ------------
+ June Brent looks set to head higher, but $18.62-$18.77 gap remains an obstacle.
+ Interim resistance for the June contract also seen around double top at $18.50.
+ Gas oil appears expected to move sideways to higher with key resistance along top of trend channel at $165.50.
IPE Brent futures were expected to head tentatively higher on Tuesday, with the gap at $18.62-$18.77 remaining the June contract's biggest obstacle, technical analysts said.
June Brent closed 27 cents higher at $18.34 per barrel on Monday, while the May contract, which expires at the end of Tuesday's session, ended 29 cents up at $18.17.
Chartists said a downside gap spanning the high of April 3 at $18.62 and the April 2 low of $18.77 would remained the June contract's biggest hurdle.
"The market needs to close the gap to $18.77," said Steve Kwan at MMS in London. "But it's to early to turn bullish or look to a break of $19 so I would put stops at $18.77 and $19."

Below there, traders also noted the double top at $18.50 seen on Monday and last Thursday, which could also be expanded to a quadruple top if the $18.49 high of April 9 and $18.53 high of April 4 are taken into account.

"I'm not surprised to see a double top there," said Kwan. "I would expect the market to put stops in just under the gap. But we've had a few days of consolidation and there's not so much downward pressure so I think a few people might push higher."
Looking on a weekly basis, Peter Sceats at Char-Tech MCS, in his weekly report, pegged medium term resistance at $19.18 in line with the upper boundary of the three-month trend channel on the chart.
While he saw ultimate support at $16.78 on a Fibonacci retracement basis. He also noted retracement levels on the $15.41 to $25.06 range of $22.78, $21.37, $20.23, $19.10 and $17.69.
On a monthly basis, he noted retracement levels at $22.19, $20.41, $18.98, $17.55 and $15.77 for the $12.90 to $25.06 range.
Sceats noted that last week the monthly Fibonacci series spotted the week's low "almost to the penny".
Gas oil meanwhile appeared to be hugging its downward trend channel drawn off the $177.50 high of March 19 and the $171.50 low of March 17.
On Monday, the May contract briefly breached the upper channel line to trade as high as $165.75 but by the end of the session it was back down at $165.00 a tonne.
-- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
